body: Your army must include at least one Wizard to be its Master of the Dead.If your army includes several Wizards, the Master of the Dead will be the one with the highest Level of Wizardry. If two or more models have the highest Wizard Level, you may choose which one is the Master of the Dead when writing your muster list. You must tell your opponent which model is your Master of the Dead before deploying your army.

Should your Master of the Dead be slain, the magical animus of the army starts to dissipate. As soon as your Master of the Dead is removed from play as a casualty, all friendly units with the Necromantic Undead special rule lose the Regeneration (X) special rule.

In addition, at the end of the phase in which your Master of the Dead was removed from play as a casualty, and during each of your Start of Turn sub-phases for the remainder of the game, all friendly units with the Necromantic Undead special rule that are currently on the battlefield must make a Leadership test. If this test is failed, the unit loses a number of Wounds equal to the amount by which it failed the test.

For example, your army’s Master of the Dead is destroyed during your opponent’s Shooting phase. At the end of that phase a unit of Skeleton Warriors (Ld 5) makes a Leadership test and rolls a 7 (failing the test by 2). That unit immediately loses two Wounds. During your next Start of Turn sub-phase, the same unit makes another Leadership test, this time rolling a 6, resulting in the loss of one Wound.

Models with this special rule are not affected if the Master of the Dead for your army is slain. Furthermore, unless they have joined a unit that does not have this special rule they (and their mounts) can march as normal. In addition, A Vampire Count or Vampire Thrall Wizard with this special rule may wear armour or carry a shield without penalty. IE: They may Cast and Dispel as Normal.

Models with this special rule are ‘Undead.’ Undead models cannot march (unless they have the Fly (X) special rule and choose to move by flying). In addition, all Undead models have the following universal special rules:
Fear • Immune to Psychology • Unbreakable • Unstable
A character with this special rule cannot join a unit without this special rule, and vice versa Invocation Of Nehek

During the Command sub-phase of their turn, if they are not engaged in combat, this character may attempt to resurrect the fallen (see page 28) by making a Leadership test (using their own Leadership). If this test is passed, a single friendly unit that has the Necromantic Undead special rule and is within 12" of this character recovers a number of lost Wounds. However, magically repairing great Undead beasts is much harder than
raising Zombies from the dirt. Therefore, how many Wounds are recovered depends upon the unit’s troop type and this character’s Level of Wizardry:

If the unit’s troop type is ‘regular infantry’ or ‘swarms,’ it recovers a number of Wounds equal to this character’s Level of Wizardry +D3. • If the unit’s troop type is ‘light cavalry’ or ‘war beasts,’ it recovers a number of Wounds equal to this character’s Level of Wizardry +1. • If the unit’s troop type is ‘heavy infantry,’ ‘monstrous infantry,’ ‘heavy cavalry,’ ‘monstrous cavalry’ or ‘light chariot,’ it recovers a number of Wounds equal to this character’s Level of Wizardry. • If the unit’s troop type is ‘heavy chariot,’ ‘monstrous creature,’ ‘behemoth’ or ‘war machine,’ it recovers a single Wound. • Models with the Dark Vitality or Ethereal special rules recover half the amount of wounds as described above (including any bonuses), rounding fractions up.
When resurrecting the fallen, a unit with this special rule can be taken beyond its starting size by an additional 20 models.

A unit comprised entirely of modes with this special rule treats all terrain as open ground for the purposes of movement. They cannot end their movement inside impassable terrain, though they can pass through it.

At the end of a Combat phase in which a unit with this special rule caused one or more unsaved wounds, roll a D6 for each unsaved wound caused. For each roll of 5+, models with this special rule recover one lost Wound, following the rules for Resurrecting the Fallen. However, a model with the Behemoth troop type may only ever recover a maximum of one Wound per phase in this manner.

In addition, if a unit with this special rule wishes to Pursue or Overrun, it must make a Leadership test. If this test is failed, the unit still Pursues or Overruns, but rolls a single D6 to determine the distance moved, rather than the usual 2D6.

A model with this special rule may make a ‘Wailing Dirge’ attack. A Wailing Dirge attack is a Shooting attack with the Magical Attacks special rule and a range of 8”. A Wailing Dirge attack can target an enemy Lone character regardless of the usual rules for targeting Lone characters. If this model is engaged in combat during the Shooting phase, it may target a unit in base contact with a Wailing Dirge attack and may do so even if it charged this turn.

A Wailing Dirge attack does not roll to hit and wound as normal. Instead, the target must make a Leadership test with a negative modifier to its Leadership characteristic shown in the brackets after the name of this special rule (shown here as ‘X’). If this test is failed, the target suffers a number of wounds equal to the amount by which it failed the test, with no armour or Regeneration saves permitted (Ward saves can be attempted as normal).
Note that a Wailing Dirge attack may reduce the target's Leadership characteristic to a minimum of 2
If a model with this special rule is your General, all Crypt Ghouls, Crypt Horrors and Vargulfs gain the Vanguard special rule.

A character that can be mounted may choose a mount from the following list. Some mounts are covered in detail on this page. Those that are not have their own dedicated entries later in this army list.

Terrorgheist See page 21

A unit with this special rule never receives an initiative bonus for charging an enemy in its front, flank or rear arc. In addition, when this unit Pursues or Overruns, roll a single D6 to determine the distance moved, rather than the usual 2D6.

At the start of the Combat phase, any enemy unit in base contact with one or more models with this special rule must make a Leadership test. If this test is failed, that unit gains the Strikes Last special rule until the end of the phase.

Whilst within the Command range of one or more models with this special rule, friendly units with the Necromantic Undead special rule gain a +1 modifier to their Movement and Initiative characteristics.

All Wizards (friend or foe) may apply a +1 modifier to any Casting roll whilst within the Command range of one or more models with this special rule. However, if any Wizard miscasts whilst within this model’s Command range, they must roll twice on the Miscast table and apply both results.
Character Mount: A Mortis Engine may only be included in your army as a character’s mount. Its points are added to that of its rider.
Enemy Wizards that are within 18" of one or more models with this special rule when attempting to cast a spell must increase that spell’s casting value by 1.

When a friendly unit that is within 12" of this model recovers a number of lost Wounds due to a character using the Invocation of Nehek special rule, roll a D6. On a roll of 4+, add +1 to the result. In addition, friendly units within 12" of one or more models with this special rule reduce the number of Wounds lost due to the Unstable special rule by 1.
Note that this is cumulative with the Indomitable (X) special rule (see page 27).

Whilst within 6" of one or more models with this special rule, friendly units of Zombies lose the Shambling Hordes special rule, gain the Newly Dead special rule, and modify their Weapon Skill characteristic by +1. In addition, whenever a friendly unit of Zombies within 6" of one or more models with this special rule recovers lost Wounds due to the Invocation of Nehek special rule, it recovers an additional D3 Wounds.

Character Mount: A Corpse Cart may be included in your army as a character's mount. If so, the Necromantic Acolyte replaces the Corpsemaster and the Corpse Cart’s points are added to that of its rider.

von-carstein-ring.body:
Vampires only. The bearer of this item has a 5+ Ward save against all wounds suffered. In addition, if the bearer loses their final Wound and is removed from play as a casualty, roll a D6. On a roll of 2+, the model is immediately returned to play. Place the model back in the exact position it occupied prior to being removed, with 1 Wound remaining.

Once this resurrection ability has been used, the Von Carstein Ring is destroyed and its effects are lost for the remainder of the game.

drakenhof-banner.body: If a unit carrying the Drakenhof Banner has the Regeneration (X+) special rule, it improves the armour value of its Regeneration save by 1.

banner-of-the-barrows.body: Cannot be taken by a unit with the Dark Vitality special rule. During the Combat phase, when a unit carrying the Banner of the Barrows makes a roll To Hit, a roll of 3+ is always a success, regardless of the target’s Weapon Skill.

the-screaming-banner.body: When an enemy unit makes a Leadership test due to Fear caused by a unit carrying the Screaming Banner, it must roll an extra D6 and discard the lowest result.

helm-of-commandment.body: Necromancers and Wights only. During the Command sub-phase of their turn, this character may attempt to enhance the sentience of those around them by making a Leadership test (using their own Leadership). If this test is passed, until your next Start of Turn sub-phase this character and any unit they have joined gains a +1 modifier to their Weapon Skill characteristic (to a maximum of 10).

hand-of-dust.body:
Necromancers and Wights only. This model can cast the following Bound spell, with a Power Level of 1. Roll a D6 each time the Hand of Dust is used. On a roll of 1, it crumbles to dust and cannot be used again:

Mercenaries: Up to 20% of your army’s points value may be spent on the following units taken as mercenaries:
Free Company Militia and Empire Archers (see the Empire of Man army list on page 59 of Forces of Fantasy)

Note that mercenary units drawn from another army list gain the Mercenaries special rule and become subject to the ‘Misbehaving Mercenaries’ rules, as described on page 279 of the Warhammer: the Old World rulebook.
Allies: Vampire Count Allies In addition to the Allies listed in Ravening Hordes, armies made using the Tomb Kings of Khemri Grand Army composition may include an Allied contingent drawn from the Vampire Counts Legacy Army composition.
